clinicalReview: Required before activation in Epic. Not the standard of care.
title: Diabetes: Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State [with or without DKA]
mission: Separate hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state, with or without DKA, from isolated DKA.
checkpoints: Check age at least 10 years and weight at least 50 kg before entering.
Apply the glucose, bicarbonate, ketone, pH, and osmolality pattern the standard uses to label HHS or mixed HHS with DKA.
Stop for parenteral-nutrition hyperglycemia, pregnancy, or drug-induced altered mental status.
mayPropose: Unsigned fluid and monitoring orders quoted from the active branch.
cardSummary: TCH hyperosmolar-state standard may apply. Confirm age, weight, and the lab pattern.

population.inclusion: Patients 10 years of age and older; Weight 50 kg or greater HHS without DKA; Plasma glucose concentration >600 mg/dL; Serum bicarbonate >15 mmol/L; Beta-hydroxybutyrate <4 mmol/L; pH >7.2; Effective serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg Mixed HHS with DKA; Plasma glucose concentration >600 mg/dL; Beta-hydroxybutyrate >4 mmol/L; pH <7.2, without other causes of low pH (i.e. lactic acidosis); Effective serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg
population.exclusion: Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) induced hyperglycemia; Pregnancy; Drug induced altered mental status

source.publisher: Texas Children's Hospital Evidence-Based Outcomes Center
source.pdf: clinical-standards/12 Diabetes Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State with or without DKA.pdf
